text: The Weyl group of the root system $A_{n-1}$ (that of $\mathfrak{sl}_n$) is isomorphic to:
explanation: For type $A_{n-1}$ the simple reflections act as the transpositions $(i\;i{+}1)$, and they generate $W \cong S_n$. The signed-permutation group $(\mathbb{Z}/2)^n\rtimes S_n$ is the Weyl group of $B_n/C_n$; the cyclic group and the alternating group $A_n$ (a pun on the type label) are not the Weyl group.
